San may accept only a literal prefix without reporting a compile error; compile success is not full-expression or behavior proof. Do not replace conditions with always-on class tokens. Do not guess dynamic keys, spreads or unmapped source scopes; keep unsupported cases explicit for review.
San data access rule: never destructure this.data or treat it as a plain object. Read fields separately, for example const initialGroups = this.data.get('initialGroups'), then write state with this.data.set(...). This also applies inside every inline child: if a Vue prop is named data, use this.data.get('data').map(...) and this.data.get('data').length, never this.data.map(...) or this.data.length. Computed values must be read with this.data.get('computedName'), not this.computedName. San computed callbacks do not receive the full component instance: never call this.getX() or any other component method inside computed; use pure helper functions with explicit data arguments. In every inline child template, on-* handlers must call component methods, not assign state directly: use on-mouseenter="setHoveredIndex(index)" with a method that calls this.data.set('hoveredIndex', index), never on-mouseenter="hoveredIndex = index".
